sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AN UPPER TROUGH CENTERED OVER ORE/ID EARLY THIS MORNING WILL EJECT EWD INTO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS BY TONIGHT AS A SECOND WAVE DIGS SEWD TOWARD THE PAC COAST. AS THIS OCCURS...MIDLEVEL HEIGHT FALLS AND 30-50 KT UPPER-LEVEL SWLYS WILL SPREAD DOWNSTREAM ACROSS THE CNTRL/NRN PLAINS. AT THE SURFACE...LOW PRESSURE WILL REMAIN ANCHORED OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS...WITH A STATIONARY FRONT EXTENDING NEWD INTO SERN SD...WHICH WILL TRANSITION INTO A WARM FRONT THAT MAY LIFT NWD INTO CNTRL MN/WI DURING THE DAY. IN ADDITION...A DRYLINE WILL EXTEND SSW FROM THE SURFACE LOW INTO ERN NM AND FAR W TX. SIMILAR TO THE PAST COUPLE OF DAYS...THE STATIONARY AND WARM FRONTAL BOUNDARIES WILL AID IN FOCUSING SCATTERED TO NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS DURING THE D1 PERIOD AS STRONG SLY FLOW TRANSPORTS A MOIST/UNSTABLE AIRMASS INTO THE FRONTAL ZONE.

sections.title: N-CNTRL HIGH PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY/UPPER MIDWEST
sections.text: AN MCS WILL BE ONGOING AT THE BEGINNING OF THE FORECAST PERIOD FROM PORTIONS OF ERN NEB INTO MN AND WI...AND MAY POSE A MARGINAL SEVERE WEATHER THREAT DURING PART OF THE MORNING. FOCUS WILL THEN TURN TO AN UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME OVER THE N-CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE IS FORECAST TO STRENGTHEN BY EARLY TO MID AFTERNOON FROM ERN WY INTO NERN CO AS A MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH EJECTS EWD TOWARD THE REGION. DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S APPEAR PROBABLE OVER ERN WY...WRN NEB...AND WRN SD...AND WILL AID IN MODERATE INSTABILITY AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZES. INITIAL STORMS WILL LIKELY BE SUPERCELLS GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF LOW-LEVEL ELY WINDS SURMOUNTED BY 40 KT MID/UPPER-LEVEL SWLYS. THESE STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE/VERY LARGE HAIL AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. STORMS OVER THE HIGH PLAINS WILL LIKELY DRIFT EWD INTO WRN/CNTRL NEB AND SWRN/S-CNTRL SD DURING THE EVENING...WITH UPSCALE GROWTH INTO AN MCS POSSIBLE. ADDITIONAL SCATTERED TO NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS ARE ALSO EXPECTED TO FORM NEWD ALONG THE STATIONARY FRONT FROM WRN NEB INTO SRN/CNTRL MN DURING THE LATE AFTERNOON AND EVENING. STRONG HEATING ALONG AND S OF THE BOUNDARY COMBINED WITH SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S TO

sections.title: SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS ARE FORECAST TO INITIATE ALONG A DRYLINE ORIENTED NE-SW FROM THE WRN TX PANHANDLE INTO FAR ERN NM AND FAR W TX. STRONG SURFACE HEATING COMBINED WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL AID IN AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES FROM 1000-2500 J/KG. VEERING WIND PROFILES WILL SUPPORT MULTICELL CLUSTERS AND A FEW SUPERCELLS POSING A THREAT FOR ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. ..GARNER/MOSIER.. 06/22/2013

sections.title: UPPER MS VALLEY THIS MORNING
sections.text: THREE LARGE COMPLEXES OF THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING THIS MORNING OVER EASTERN NEB...EASTERN IA/SOUTHWEST WI...AND NORTHERN IL. EACH OF THESE MCS/S HAVE AN ASSOCIATED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY SURGING SOUTHWARD. WHILE ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS ARE NOT LIKELY WITH THIS MORNING ACTIVITY...THE EVENTUAL PLACEMENT OF THESE BOUNDARIES WILL PLAY A MAJOR ROLE IN DETERMINING THE PRIMARY RISK AREAS FOR SEVERE STORMS LATER TODAY.

sections.title: NEB/SERN SD/SRN MN/WI
sections.text: ONE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY CURRENTLY EXTENDS FROM EASTERN NEB INTO NORTHEAST CO. SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY VERY MOIST/UNSTABLE CONDITIONS WILL DEVELOP BY MID AFTERNOON. INCREASING SOUTHERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS WILL HELP SHIFT THE BOUNDARY SLOWLY NORTHWARD...AS WELL AS FOCUS LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE LATER TODAY. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WILL FORM ALONG THIS BOUNDARY BY LATE AFTERNOON OVER NEB AND SOUTHEASTERN SD. INITIAL STORMS MAY BE SUPERCELLULAR WITH A RISK OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES. STORMS WILL EVENTUALLY GROW UPSCALE AND TRACK EASTWARD ACROSS IA AND SOUTHERN MN THIS EVENING...AND POSSIBLY INTO WI OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: HIGH PLAINS FROM SOUTHEAST MT INTO WESTERN KS
sections.text: STRONG DAYTIME HEATING AND WEAK UPSLOPE FLOW WILL PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS AGAIN TODAY OVER THE HIGH PLAINS OF SOUTHEAST MT...EASTERN WY/CO...AND WESTERN KS. SUFFICIENTLY STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL PROMOTE SUPERCELL STORMS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND ISOLATED TORNADOES. COVERAGE OF STORMS IS UNCERTAIN ON THE SOUTH END OF THIS RISK AREA /OVER CO AND KS/. HOWEVER...MULTIPLE MODELS SHOW A SIGNAL FOR AT LEAST A FEW STORMS THIS FAR SOUTH. STORMS MAY PERSIST THROUGH MUCH OF THE EVENING OVER WESTERN AND CENTRAL SD/NEB. ..HART/ROGERS.. 06/22/2013

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: TO THE SOUTH OF A REMNANT BLOCKING PATTERN OVER WESTERN AND CENTRAL CANADA...A MODEST BELT OF WESTERLIES CONTINUES TO CURVE ACROSS THE PACIFIC COAST THROUGH THE ROCKIES. A NUMBER OF SHORT WAVE TROUGHS ARE EMBEDDED WITHIN THE REGIME...INCLUDING ONE SIGNIFICANT IMPULSE NOW TURNING EASTWARD INTO THE NORTHERN/CENTRAL ROCKIES. THIS LATTER FEATURE IS EXPECTED TO PROGRESS NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE ROCKIES INTO THE NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS BY EARLY SUNDAY...PRECEDED BY AT LEAST A COUPLE OF SMALLER SCALE IMPULSES WITHIN INCREASINGLY CYCLONIC SOUTHWESTERLY MID/UPPER FLOW ACROSS THE NORTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS. MEANWHILE...A COUPLE OF PERTURBATIONS...NOW PROGRESSING INTO BROADER SCALE ANTICYCLONIC FLOW ACROSS THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO THE GREAT LAKES...WILL CONTINUE EASTWARD TODAY...AND THE TENDENCY MAY BE FOR MID-LEVEL HEIGHTS TO RISE ACROSS THE UPPER MIDWEST...BEFORE FALLING MORE SUBSTANTIVELY AGAIN LATE TONIGHT INTO SUNDAY. THIS EVOLVING PATTERN IS AGAIN EXPECTED TO SUPPORT CONSIDERABLE THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY TODAY AND TONIGHT ACROSS THE NORTHERN ROCKIES INTO THE UPPER MIDWEST...WITH INCREASING CHANCES FOR THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY ALSO EASTWARD ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES REGION INTO PARTS OF TH

sections.title: NRN/CNTRL ROCKIES EASTWARD TO UPPER MIDWEST
sections.text: THE DETAILS OF POTENTIAL CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT FOR TODAY REMAIN A BIT UNCLEAR. THE PRIMARY SURFACE BOUNDARY OF INTEREST APPEARS TO BE A COMPOSITE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY GENERATED BY STORM CLUSTERS OF THE PAST COUPLE OF DAYS...WHICH NOW GENERALLY EXTENDS ACROSS LOWER MICHIGAN...NORTHERN INDIANA AND ILLINOIS...THROUGH SOUTHERN IOWA...AND THE VICINITY OF THE KANSAS/NEBRASKA BORDER...INTO THE COLORADO FRONT RANGE. MODIFICATION AND NORTHWARD RETREAT OF THIS BOUNDARY IS UNCERTAIN...BUT STEEPEST MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...EAST OF THE HIGH PLAINS...HAVE GENERALLY BECOME FOCUSED IN A CORRIDOR ALONG AND TO ITS NORTH. MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES REMAIN MODESTLY STEEP NORTHWARD THROUGH MUCH OF THE DAKOTAS...BUT CONSIDERABLE OVERTURNING HAS STABILIZED A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY AND UPPER GREAT LAKES REGION. WHERE MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES REMAIN STEEP...THE BOUNDARY LAYER ALSO REMAINS MOIST TO THE NORTH OF THE FRONT...BENEATH MODEST SOUTHWESTERLY MID-LEVEL FLOW...WHICH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SUFFICIENT SHEAR FOR ORGANIZED STORM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS A BROAD AREA OF THE NORTH CENTRAL U.S. BY LATE AFTERNOON. IN ADDITION TO THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY...THE LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME ACROSS THE NORT

sections.title: SOUTHERN GREAT LAKES REGION/OHIO VALLEY
sections.text: MODERATE BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION DOES APPEAR PROBABLE WITH DAYTIME HEATING...ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS THE SOUTHERN GREAT LAKES REGION INTO THE OHIO VALLEY. THIS MAY BE ENOUGH TO SUPPORT SMALL CLUSTERS OF STORMS WITH AT LEAST LOW PROBABILITIES FOR SEVERE WIND/HAIL. HOWEVER...DUE TO THE WEAK NATURE OF THE FLOW FIELDS...SEVERE POTENTIAL STILL APPEARS TOO LOW FOR A SLIGHT RISK AT THE PRESENT TIME. ..KERR/BUNTING.. 06/22/2013

sections.title: SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: PRIMARY OUTLOOK ADJUSTMENT IS THE ADDITION OF A CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK FOR HAIL/WIND POTENTIAL ACROSS PARTS OF WEST/NORTHWEST TX...WITH MORE ISOLATED STORMS ALSO ANTICIPATED ACROSS FAR SOUTHWEST TX. AIDED BY A WEAK MID-LEVEL IMPULSE APPROACHING FROM NM/SOUTHERN CO...AT LEAST ISOLATED INSTANCES OF HAIL/WIND ARE EXPECTED ESPECIALLY LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING.

sections.title: ELSEWHERE
sections.text: SEE PRIOR OUTLOOK DISCUSSION BELOW AND EXISTING/SUBSEQUENT MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS. ..GUYER.. 06/22/2013 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1126 AM CDT SAT JUN 22 2013/

sections.title: CNTRL/NRN PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: COMPLEX PATTERN IS ANALYZED AT THE SURFACE THIS EVENING OVER THE CNTRL/NRN PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY. AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE WAS SITUATED OVER NERN CO...WITH A QUASI-STATIONARY FRONTAL BOUNDARY/DEEPER BAROCLINIC ZONE EXTENDING ENEWD TOWARD ERN NEB/WRN IA...WHERE IT THEN TRANSITIONS INTO A WARM FRONT THAT EXTENDS INTO FAR SERN MN AND SRN WI. DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S TO MID 70S RESIDE ALONG THE BOUNDARY....WITH TEMPERATURES IN THE 70S N OF THE FRONT AND 90S TO ITS S. ELSEWHERE...A COLD FRONT WAS ANALYZED FROM NRN ND SWWD INTO SWRN SD AND ERN WY. DEWPOINTS E OF THE FRONT OVER THE DAKOTAS ARE IN THE MID 60S...WHICH IS SUPPORTING MLCAPE VALUES UPWARDS OF 1500 J/KG DUE TO THE ONGOING PRESENCE OF AN EML/STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES. THE COMBINATION OF STRONG FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH AN UPPER DISTURBANCE EXITING THE GREAT BASIN AND THE MOIST UNSTABLE AIRMASS OVER THE DAKOTAS MAY AID IN MAINTAINING A BOWING MCS THAT WILL MOVE FROM WRN SD INTO CNTRL/ERN PORTIONS OF THE STATE OVERNIGHT. ADDITIONAL STRONG/SEVERE STORMS WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE OVER ND AS THE UPPER TROUGH APPROACHES THE COLD FRONT. FARTHER S...A COUPLE OF SUPERCELLS ARE MOVING EWD OVER THE NEB PANHANDLE AND NERN CO.

sections.title: SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: EVENING SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS A DRYLINE EXTENDING SWD FROM SERN CO INTO THE WRN TX PANHANDLE...THE PERMIAN BASIN...AND THE ERN TRANS-PECOS REGION. DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S TO NEAR 60F ARE PRESENT E OF THE BOUNDARY...WITH WARM SURFACE TEMPERATURES AND STEEP LAPSE RATES AIDING IN MLCAPE VALUES NEAR 1500 J/KG. ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED OFF OF THE DRYLINE EARLY THIS EVENING...POSSIBLY AIDED BY GLANCING LARGE-SCALE ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH AN UPPER TROUGH EXITING THE GREAT BASIN. HOWEVER...00Z AMA AND MAF RAOBS SHOW CINH IS FAIRLY SUBSTANTIAL OVER THE AREA...WHICH IS PRECLUDING GREATER STORM COVERAGE. THUS...DESPITE THE PRESENCE OF STRONG INSTABILITY AND VEERING DEEP-LAYER WIND PROFILES...SVR WEATHER THREAT IS EXPECTED TO DIMINISH RAPIDLY DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER CONTINUES TO STABILIZE. ..GARNER.. 06/23/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO INCREASE IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY OVER INTERIOR WYOMING THIS MORNING INTO THE AFTERNOON. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS. DEPENDING ON CONVECTIVE TRENDS...A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH MIGHT BE NEEDED BY 17Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATE THIS MORNING VISIBLE IMAGERY INDICATES A LARGE AREA OF MOSTLY CLEAR SKIES OVER CNTRL WY WITH UPPER 40S DEWPOINTS IN PLACE. FURTHER DIABATIC WARMING SHOULD BOOST TEMPERATURES TO NEAR 70 WITH STEEP LAPSE RATES AND 500 J/KG MLCAPE. A COUPLE OF CONVECTIVELY ACTIVE CONVERGENCE BANDS WERE ALSO INDICATED...ONE LIFTING THROUGH NERN WY AND ANOTHER FARTHER WEST FROM NEAR RIVERTON TO GREYBULL. THIS BAND OF DEEPER CONVERGENCE AND ASCENT EXISTS DOWNSTREAM FROM A VORTICITY MAXIMUM LOCATED OVER SRN ID WITHIN BASE OF A PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH. CONVECTION WITHIN THIS BAND MAY INTENSIFY AS IT SHIFTS THROUGH THE DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS CNTRL WY. OTHER STORMS MAY INITIATE OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF SWRN WY AND SPREAD NEWD. RIVERTON 12Z RAOB INDICATED 60 KT OF SFC-6 KM SHEAR THAT WILL PROMOTE SUPERCELLS ONCE SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY IS REALIZED BY THE DEVELOPING UPDRAFTS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WIDELY SCATTERED STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP OVER THE MOUNTAINS OF NCTRL CO AND SUBSEQUENTLY MOVE INTO THE HIGH PLAINS OF NERN CO THIS AFTERNOON. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS. TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WW ISSUANCE BY 20Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: EARLY THIS AFTERNOON SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS CUMULUS DEVELOPMENT OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF NCNTRL CO. THE CIRCULATION AROUND A SFC LOW OVER NWRN KS IS RESULTING IN ENELY LOW-LEVEL WINDS WHICH WILL MAINTAIN INFLUX OF LOW-MID 50S DEWPOINTS OVER THE HIGH PLAINS OF NERN CO AND A MODEST UPSLOPE COMPONENT. STRONG DIABATIC WARMING IS DESTABILIZING THE SFC LAYER...AND LATEST OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS SHOWS MLCAPE FROM 1000-1500 J/KG. BASED ON MODIFIED 12Z RAOBS AND POINT FORECAST SOUNDINGS...TEMPERATURES IN THE MID-UPPER 80 F ARE NEEDED TO SUSTAIN ROBUST THUNDERSTORMS EAST OF THE HIGHER TERRAIN. THIS SUGGESTS ANOTHER 1.5 - 2 HOURS OF INSOLATION IS NEEDED OVER THE NERN CO HIGH PLAINS BEFORE STORMS BEGIN TO POSE A SEVERE THREAT. THE 30-35 KT SWLY FLOW AT 500 MB ABOVE LIGHT ELY NEAR SFC WINDS IS CONTRIBUTING TO 40-45 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR THAT WILL FAVOR A FEW SUPERCELLS ONCE STORMS DEVELOP AND ROOT INTO THE BOUNDARY LAYER.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WIND AND ISOLATED TORNADOES PERSISTS ACROSS WW 343 WITH THE PRIMARY THREAT NEXT COUPLE HOURS EXPECTED FROM CNTRL THROUGH ERN WY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUE DEVELOPING OVER THE MOUNTAINS FROM WCNTRL THROUGH SERN WY INCLUDING THE LARAMIE RANGE. A CORRIDOR OF RELATIVELY HIGHER INSTABILITY EXISTS FROM ECNTRL THROUGH SERN WY WHERE STRONG DIABATIC WARMING AND MOIST LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE FLOW EXISTS SUPPORTING MLCAPE FROM 1000-1500 J/KG. STORMS WILL LIKELY PERSIST AS DISCRETE SUPERCELLS AND OCCASIONAL BOWING SEGMENTS NEXT COUPLE HOURS WITHIN A KINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY VEERING LOW LEVEL WINDS AND 35-45 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR. CHARACTER OF CLOUDS IN NERN WY SUGGESTS THE BOUNDARY LAYER IS STILL CAPPED...BUT FURTHER DIABATIC WARMING MAY PROMOTE DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINED THUNDERSTORMS BY 21Z. ..DIAL.. 06/22/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS EXPECTED TO MOVE/DEVELOP INTO THE HIGH PLAINS OF WRN NEB THROUGH THE WRN DAKOTAS AFTER 21Z. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS...BUT A COUPLE TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: DIABATIC WARMING OVER THE HIGH PLAINS OF WRN NEB INTO WRN SD IS DESTABILIZING THE BOUNDARY LAYER WITHIN A MOIST LOW-LEVEL ELY UPSLOPE REGIME. LATEST OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS INDICATES 1500-2000 J/KG MLCAPE ALREADY IN PLACE. NUMEROUS STORMS HAVE DEVELOPED OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WY WITHIN A ZONE OF FAVORABLE LARGE SCALE ASCENT DOWNSTREAM FROM A PROGRESSIVE UPPER TROUGH. THIS ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY CONTINUE DEVELOPING EWD INTO THE HIGH PLAINS SUPPORTED BY AN INCREASINGLY UNSTABLE BOUNDARY LAYER. SOME INCREASE IN SWLY MID-LEVEL WINDS IS EXPECTED AS THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH ADVANCES FARTHER EAST WITH EFFECTIVE SHEAR FROM 40-50 KT FAVORING ORGANIZED STORMS. FEW SUPERCELLS APPEAR LIKELY...BUT THERE MAY BE A TENDENCY FOR SOME OF THE STORMS TO GROW UPSCALE INTO CLUSTERS. IF STORMS CAN REMAIN DISCRETE THE POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED TORNADOES WOULD BE GREATER...OTHERWISE DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY THREATS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTM DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE OVER PORTIONS OF CENTRAL NEB DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. IF TSTMS DO DEVELOP...CONDITIONS WOULD BE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS AND A WW WOULD BE NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM OVERNIGHT CONVECTION HAS BECOME THE EFFECTIVE FRONTAL BOUNDARY OVER NEB AND AT 20Z EXTENDED FROM NR IMPERIAL TO COLUMBUS. THE FRONT HAS LIFTED NWD ALLOWING A VERY MOIST LOW-LEVEL SLY FLOW TO DEVELOP WITH MID-UPPER 60S DEW POINTS NEAR THE BOUNDARY. STRONG DIABATIC HEATING HAS COMBINED WITH THE INCREASING MOISTURE TO RESULT IN MLCAPE VALUES BETWEEN 2000 AND LOCALLY 3000 J/KG IN THE VICINITY OF THE FRONT. THE DISCUSSION AREA IS ALONG THE SRN FRINGE OF STRONGER MID-TROPOSPHERIC SWLY FLOW AVERAGING 35 KTS...AND AS A RESULT EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 35 TO 40 KTS EXISTS ACROSS THE AREA. LATEST VIS SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS AN INCREASING CU FIELD ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE FRONT WHICH CORRESPONDS WITH OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS SHOWING DIMINISHING MLCINH IN THIS AREA. THERE IS SOME UNCERTAINTY ON THE EXACT TIMING OF CONVECTIVE INITIATION...WITH TSTM DEVELOPMENT BECOMING MORE PROBABLE TOWARDS EVENING. ONCE STORMS DEVELOP THE ENVIRONMENT FAVORS SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS AND POSSIBLY A TORNADO...ESPECIALLY IN THE VICINITY OF THE FRONTAL BOUNDARY. THIS AREA WILL BE MONITORED FOR SIGNS OF TSTM DEVELOPMENT. ALTHOUGH A WATCH IS POSSIBLE IN THE SHORT TERM...THE LIKELIHOOD INCREASES TOWARDS LATE AFTN/EARLY EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE RISK MAY INCREASE THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING IN AREAS INCLUDING SOUTHEAST MN/NORTHEAST IA INTO WESTERN WI. THIS INCLUDES THE POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. CONVECTIVE TRENDS ARE BEING CLOSELY MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: PER VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY...TOWERING CU IS NOTED IN VICINITY OF AN EFFECTIVE FRONTAL ZONE THAT ANGLES ACROSS SOUTHEAST MN/NORTHEAST IA INTO SOUTHWEST WI...WITH A FEW INCIPIENT TSTMS NOW NOTED AS WELL. THE AIRMASS ALONG/SOUTHWEST OF THIS FRONTAL BOUNDARY HAS BECOME QUITE UNSTABLE...WITH MLCAPE LIKELY ON THE ORDER OF 2000-3000+ J/KG AS LOW-LEVEL INHIBITION CONTINUES TO ERODE AND BECOME INCREASINGLY NEGLIGIBLE. ESPECIALLY GIVEN THE APPROACH OF AN UPSTREAM MID-LEVEL IMPULSE/POSSIBLE MCV ACROSS FAR SOUTHERN MN/NORTHWEST IA...ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT SEEMS PROBABLE THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. A RIBBON SOMEWHAT STRONGER MID-LEVEL FLOW IS LIKELY TIED TO THIS IMPULSE...SUCH THAT ORGANIZED MULTICELLS AND A FEW SUPERCELLS MAY BE POSSIBLE...ESPECIALLY GIVEN THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY AND THE PRESENCE OF THE FRONTAL BOUNDARY. CONVECTIVE TRENDS ARE BEING CLOSELY MONITORED AND INCREASING TRENDS MAY PROMPT A WATCH ISSUANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD INCREASE OVER NERN CO OVER THE NEXT 1 TO 2 HOURS. THE THREAT SHOULD EVENTUALLY MOVE INTO SWRN NEB. WIND DAMAGE...LARGE HAIL AND AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT WILL BE POSSIBLE. WW ISSUANCE WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED ACROSS THE REGION BY 23Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE INITIATED JUST TO THE EAST OF THE FRONT RANGE OVER THE LAST HOUR. THESE STORMS WILL MOVE NEWD INTO MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY LOCATED ACROSS NERN CO AND SW NEB. THE PLATTEVILLE PROFILER CURRENTLY SHOWS ABOUT 30 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR. THIS COMBINED WITH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE STORMS WITH LARGE HAIL. AS THE CELLS MOVE NEWD INTO A MORE FAVORABLE SHEAR AND MOISTURE ENVIRONMENT ACROSS NE CO AND SW NEB WHERE 0-6 KM SHEAR IS ESTIMATED AT 40 TO 45 KT AND SFC DEWPOINTS ARE NEAR 60 F...SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT WILL BE LIKELY. THE STORMS SHOULD BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING ISOLATED VERY LARGE HAIL...WIND DAMAGE AND A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTM INITIATION IS EXPECTED WITHIN AN HOUR OR SO WITH TSTM COVERAGE THEN INCREASING FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. SVR TSTMS ARE ANTICIPATED AND A WW MAY BE NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY REVEALS AN INCREASINGLY AGITATED CU FIELD ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE TX PANHANDLE WITH SOME CU DEVELOPMENT NOTED ACROSS THE TX SOUTH PLAINS AND SW TX NOTED AS WELL. SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACES A LEE LOW ACROSS SE CO WITH A DRYLINE EXTENDING SWD TO JUST W OF AMA THEN SWWD TO INK /IN SW TX/. THE ENVIRONMENT E OF THE DRYLINE IS CHARACTERIZED BY TEMPERATURES IN THE MID 90S AND DEWPOINTS GENERALLY IN THE UPPER 50S. THIS WARM AND MOIST LOW-LEVEL ENVIRONMENT EXISTS BENEATH VERY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES /AOA 8.5 DEG C PER KG/...PROMOTING MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY ACROSS THE REGION. BULK SHEAR SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT ROTATING STORMS. AN EXPANSIVE CIRRUS SHIELD CONTINUES TO MOVE THROUGH THE REGION...LIMITING HEATING. HOWEVER...FORECAST SOUNDINGS AND MESOANALYSIS INDICATE LITTLE TO NO CINH REMAINS. AS SUCH...TSTM INITIATION IS EXPECTED SOON WITH AN INCREASE IN TSTM COVERAGE EXPECTED THROUGH THE EVENING. GIVEN THE ENVIRONMENT...SVR TSTMS ARE EXPECTED WITH PRIMARY THREATS OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED AND A WW MAY BE NEEDED OVER PORTIONS OF THE AREA.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE THREAT WILL LIKELY INCREASE ACROSS NRN AND CNTRL SD OVER THE NEXT 1 TO 2 HOURS. WIND DAMAGE AND ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE. WW ISSUANCE WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED ACROSS THE REGION AROUND 01Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH ACROSS ERN WY WITH A 40 TO 50 KT SPEED MAX ANALYZED OVER CNTRL WY. LIFT ASSOCIATED WITH THE SHORTWAVE AND MODERATE INSTABILITY LOCATED ACROSS WCNTRL SD WILL HELP FUEL A BOWING LINE-SEGMENT EWD INTO NCNTRL SD. MLCAPE IS ESTIMATED IN THE 1500 TO 2000 J/KG RANGE ACROSS THE MCD AREA WITH REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS SHOWING ABOUT 40 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR. THIS ENVIRONMENT SHOULD SUPPORT A SEVERE THREAT WITH THE BOW. WIND DAMAGE WILL BE GREATEST THREAT BUT ISOLATED LARGE HAIL MAY ALSO OCCUR WITH THE MORE INTENSE CELLS EMBEDDED IN THE LINE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS TORNADO WATCHES 344...346...AND 347. AN INCREASING LLJ WILL PROMOTE A CONTINUED TORNADO THREAT. SOME POTENTIAL EXIST FOR UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A BOWING MCS LATER TONIGHT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACES A COMPOSITE FRONTAL BOUNDARY FROM FAR SW NEB/NW KS NEWD ACROSS CNTRL NEB INTO W-CNTRL IA AND INTO FAR SW WI. THIS BOUNDARY IS EFFECTIVELY ACTING AS A WARM FRONT ACROSS NEB WITH TEMPERATURES SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY IN THE UPPER 80S TO LOW 90S AND SLY WINDS AROUND 10-20 KT WHILE TEMPERATURES NORTH OF THE BOUNDARY ARE THE UPPER 70S TO LOW 80S AND WINDS WERE ELY. THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY HAS GENERALLY REMAINED ISOLATED WITH THE EXCEPTION OF A BOWING LINE SEGMENT ACROSS THE NEB PANHANDLE. LLJ IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE ACROSS THE PLAINS DURING THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. THIS INCREASE WILL ENLARGE HODOGRAPHS...PROMOTING A CONTINUED TORNADO THREAT...PARTICULARLY IN THE VICINITY OF THE BOUNDARY ACROSS NEB. ADDITIONALLY...THE INCREASED LLJ WILL ENCOURAGE WAA WITH RESULTANT ELEVATED TSTM DEVELOPMENT EXPECTED N OF THE BOUNDARY ACROSS N-CNTRL NEB. FARTHER W...LINE OF TSTMS ACROSS THE NEB PANHANDLE IS GENERALLY MOVING SEWD WHILE THE CLUSTER OVER NE CO MOVES ENEWD. INTERACTION BETWEEN THESE TWO TSTM AREAS IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE WAA ACTIVITY AND THE FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS NEB IS EXPECTED TO PROMOTE UPSCALE GROWTH INTO BOWING MCS. MOST LIKELY TRACK APPEARS TO BE ACROSS WW 347 IN CNTRL NEB. 00Z LBF SOUNDING SAMPLED A VERY UNSTABLE AND SUFFICIENTLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT CAPABLE OF SUPPORTING ALL SVR WEATHER THREATS. ..MOSIER.. 06/23/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE THREAT ACROSS NE NEB...SE SD...NCNTRL IA AND SRN MN IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR TORNADOES ALONG WITH LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS. WW ISSUANCE WILL BE NEEDED BY 02Z ACROSS THE REGION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A FRONTAL BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM SCNTRL NEB ENEWD ACROSS NRN IA. SFC WINDS ARE BACKED TO THE NORTH OF THE BOUNDARY WITH SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S TO NEAR 70 F. THIS COMBINED WITH MODERATE DEEP LAYER SHEAR SHOULD BE FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE STORMS AS CELLS EXPAND IN COVERAGE AND MOVE EWD ALONG THE INSTABILITY GRADIENT. SUPERCELLS SHOULD BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE. AS THE LOW-LEVEL JET EXPANDS ACROSS THE REGION LATER THIS EVENING...A FEW TORNADOES ALSO MAY OCCUR WITH THE MORE DOMINANT SUPERCELLS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A NEW WW WILL BE NEEDED TO REPLACE WW 345 /WHICH EXPIRES AT 03Z/. THE NEW WATCH WILL NEED TO INCLUDE PORTIONS OF ERN ND AS THE LINE OF TSTMS IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE NEWD INTO THE AREA. DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREAT BUT A FEW EMBEDDED TORNADOES ARE ALSO POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MATURE LINEAR MCS CONTINUES NEWD ACROSS N-CNTRL SD AND S-CNTRL ND. RECENT RADAR IMAGERY HAS SHOWN AN INCREASE IN FORWARD PROPAGATION...LIKELY A RESULT OF INTERACTION BETWEEN THE MCS AND A FRONTAL BOUNDARY WHICH EXTENDS FROM N-CNTRL ND SWWD INTO SWRN SD. ADDITIONALLY...ACTIVITY AHEAD OF THE LINE TO THE E OF BIS HAS SHOWN AN INCREASING TREND. BASED ON THE 00Z BIS SOUNDING AND THE NWWD MOTION OF THE STORMS...THIS ACTIVITY IS LIKELY SURFACE OR NEAR-SURFACE BASED. INTERACTION BETWEEN THE ONGOING MCS AND THESE TSTMS WILL LIKELY RESULT IN FURTHER FORWARD PROPAGATION OF MCS. ANOTHER FACTOR FAVORING CONTINUATION OF THE MCS IS THE APPROACHING SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND SUBTLE IMPULSE AHEAD OF IT. SATELLITE IMAGERY REVEALS THAT THE PRIMARY SHORTWAVE TROUGH REMAINS FARTHER W ACROSS WRN WY. HOWEVER...THERE ARE INDICATIONS WITHIN MODEL GUIDANCE THAT A SUBTLE IMPULSE EXISTS AHEAD OF THE PRIMARY SHORTWAVE TROUGH. THE TSTM ACTIVITY E OF BIS INCREASES THE CONFIDENCE THAT SUCH A FEATURE EXISTS. AS A RESULT...A SVR THREAT IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE PAST THE CURRENT WATCH EXPIRATION TIME OF 03Z AND WILL EXTEND FARTHER E INTO ERN ND. AS SUCH...A NEW WW WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED. PRIMARY THREAT IS DAMAGING WINDS ALTHOUGH A TORNADOES EMBEDDED WITHIN THE LINE ARE ALSO POSSIBLE...ESPECIALLY ON THE NRN END OF THE LINE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE THREAT ACROSS WW 347 WILL LIKELY SPREAD EWD INTO CNTRL AND ERN NEB OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT WILL EXIST ALONG WITH A POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WITH THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS STILL SHOWS A WELL-DEFINED FRONTAL BOUNDARY EXTENDING ENEWD FROM SCNTRL NEB INTO NERN NEB. SFC DEWPOINTS ALONG THE BOUNDARY ARE NEAR 70 F AND MODERATE INSTABILITY IS IN PLACE WITH MLCAPE IN THE 2000 TO 3000 J/KG RANGE. IN ADDITION...REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS SHOW 40 TO 45 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR AS WAS ALSO EVIDENT ON THE NORTH PLATTE 00Z SOUNDING EARLIER THIS EVENING. THE SOUNDING SHOWED A 700 TO 500 MB LAPSE RATE NEAR 8.5 C/KM SUGGESTING THE ACTIVITY MOVING INTO CNTRL NEB SHOULD CONTAIN A LARGE HAIL THREAT. AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT COULD ALSO DEVELOP AS THE CELLS INTERACT WITH A LOW-LEVEL JET OVER SCNTRL NEB. WIND DAMAGE WILL BE LIKELY ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF THE LINE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE THREAT WILL CONTINUE ACROSS WW 349 AND SHOULD INCREASE FROM WEST TO EAST OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. WIND DAMAGE AND HAIL WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREATS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LONG-LIVED COMPLEX OF STORMS IS MOVING ACROSS SE SD. THE STORMS ARE LOCATED JUST TO THE NORTH OF A TRIPLE POINT WHERE A COLD FRONT...JUST BEHIND THE LINE OF STORMS...CROSSES ANOTHER STATIONARY BOUNDARY EXTENDING EWD ACROSS NRN IA. SFC DEWPOINTS ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY ARE IN THE UPPER 60S TO NEAR 70 F WITH MLCAPE ESTIMATED IN THE 1000 TO 2000 J/KG RANGE. THIS COMBINED WITH 35 TO 40 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND THE VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER SHOULD BE FAVORABLE FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. THE MORE INTENSE CELLS EMBEDDED IN THE LINE SHOULD ALSO HAVE A THREAT FOR HAIL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SVR WEATHER THREAT PERSISTS ACROSS NORTH CENTRAL ND...WITH THE STRONGEST ACTIVITY --- THOUGH WEAKENING WITH TIME --- WILL MOVE N OF THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER BY 08Z. THUS...WW 350 COULD BE CANCELLED EARLY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 0615Z...REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED A LINE OF STORMS IN NORTH CENTRAL ND...EXTENDING FROM ROLETTE COUNTY TO WRN RAMSEY COUNTY. THIS ACTIVITY WAS THE REMAINING SVR WEATHER THREAT FOR WW 350...AND GIVEN A N/NEWD MOVEMENT AT 30 KT THESE STORMS SHOULD EXIT ND INTO ADJACENT SRN MANITOBA AROUND 08Z. RESIDUAL MODERATE INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 30-40 KT MAY PROVE FAVORABLE YET FOR AN ISOLATED HAIL AND/OR STRONG WIND GUST. HOWEVER...OVERALL SEVERE WEATHER THREAT APPEARS TO BE WANING AS LIGHTNING TRENDS ARE DECREASING AND ATTENDANT CLOUD TOP TEMPERATURES ARE WARMING PER IR SATELLITE IMAGERY. ..PETERS.. 06/23/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ADDITIONAL TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ACROSS SRN AND CENTRAL MN DURING THE PRE-DAWN HOURS THROUGH 12-13Z. ALTHOUGH A FEW STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS CANNOT BE RULED OUT...TRENDS AND GUIDANCE SUGGEST THE POTENTIAL FOR AN ORGANIZED SEVERE WEATHER THREAT SHOULD REMAIN QUITE LOW. THUS...TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED...BUT NEW WW ISSUANCE IS NOT EXPECTED THROUGH 12-13Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 0810Z...MOSAIC RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED A LINEAR MCS ADVANCING EWD EARLY THIS MORNING FROM THE MID MO VALLEY INTO THE UPPER MIDWEST. THE LEADING EDGE OF THE CONVECTIVE LINE EXTENDED FROM FAR WEST CENTRAL-SWRN MN INTO FAR NWRN IA AND THEN TRAILED SWWD THROUGH ERN TO SRN NEB. A SYNOPTIC WARM FRONT EXTENDED SEWD FROM A NERN SD LOW PRESSURE AREA INTO WEST CENTRAL MN...AND THEN NEWD THROUGH EAST CENTRAL MN /NORTH SIDE OF THE TWIN CITIES METRO/ INTO NWRN WI TO WRN UPPER MI. A 50-60 KT SSWLY LLJ EXTENDING INTO SWRN MN IS MAINTAINING STRONG LOW LEVEL MASS CONVERGENCE INTO THIS REGION ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE WARM FRONT...WHILE OBJECTIVE ANALYSES SHOWED A WAA REGIME ALONG AND N OF A COMPOSITE CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WHICH EXTENDED WNWWD FROM EAST CENTRAL TO NWRN IA. THIS LOW LEVEL FORCING FOR ASCENT COMBINED WITH LARGE SCALE ASCENT WITH A PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING FROM ERN SD INTO CENTRAL/SRN MN BY 12Z WILL SUPPORT ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT WITHIN A MODERATELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT. THIS LATTER SCENARIO IS LIKELY UNDERWAY GIVEN AN INCREASE IN TSTM DEVELOPMENT AND COOLING CLOUD TOPS OVER CENTRAL MN /MCLEOD TO NICOLLET COUNTIES/. A 50 KT SWLY MIDLEVEL JET ACCOMPANYING THE ERN SD TROUGH AND A STRONG LLJ WILL MAINTAIN EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR SUFFICIENT FOR STORM ORGANIZATION...THOUGH THE ELEVATED NATURE OF THIS ACTIVITY WOULD SUGGEST HAIL WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREAT.
